properties.description:
Anthony's word, 2026-09-12: "I want to continue with implementing /feedback." The first increment after the five ordered on 2026-09-11 (430–434, all arrived).

IN: (1) the server appends one line per tool call to a usage ledger beside the design's store — tool, outcome class, refusal class where refused, duration, timestamp, harness name/version, seat — never an argument, a node id or a message; nothing is written for an in-memory design; a write that fails never fails the call. (2) A read tool that renders the ledger since the previous report (or a named date): calls by tool, never-called served tools, refusals by class and tool, skills fetched, harnesses seen, plus the metadata the server knows — reflow2 version, OS and architecture, protocol revision, design size — and writes a report marker so the next report starts after it. (3) A served skill `feedback` with the `/feedback` shortcut and its command file in the kit for every harness: it calls the tool, adds the agent's self-reported model labelled as self-reported, invites one line of disposition per refusal row, appends the whole to the project's own feedback file and shows it to the person — never sends it anywhere. (4) Tests shown to fail first: the ledger holds the verbs and never the objects; a refused call is classed, not quoted; an in-memory service writes nothing; the report covers exactly the window since the marker; the skill and command pass skill_lint and the kit manifest check; the new tool is found by a query in the user's words.

NOT IN: telemetry of any kind (nothing leaves the machine); a per-session unit in shared mode (the unit is the project, since the last report — decided, see the requirement); the refusal ledger as graph NODES (never in the design); capturing failures outside reflow2's sight (shell, git, CI — report-friction stays the form); the notepad and serve-the-lesson-at-the-step ideas from the same day's thread, which remain open.
properties.name: Increment 437 — feedback is a computed tally
